name: Zigzags
description: You are given an array $$$a_1, a_2 \dots a_n$$$. Calculate the number of tuples $$$(i, j, k, l)$$$ such that: $$$1 \le i \lt j \lt k \lt l \le n$$$; $$$a_i = a_k$$$ and $$$a_j = a_l$$$;
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 100$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$4 \le n \le 3000$$$) — the size of the array $$$a$$$. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the array $$$a$$$. It's guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ in one test doesn't exceed $$$3000$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print the number of described tuples.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1400D — Zigzags [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
